name: current_network
summary: Report this Mac's place on the local network: the active interface, its IPv4 address, this device's MAC (hardware) address, the subnet mask, how many devices the subnet can hold, and the default gateway/router IP. Use this first when diagnosing connectivity — it tells you who you are and which router to test against.

name: dns_servers
summary: List the DNS resolver (name server) IP addresses this Mac is currently using. Useful when a host pings by IP but names won't resolve — that points at DNS rather than the link.

name: ping_host
summary: Ping a host (IP address or hostname) to test reachability, and report packet loss and round-trip time. Works for LAN devices (e.g. the router or a printer), public IPs, and hostnames. To diagnose 'no internet', ping the gateway from current_network, then a public IP such as 8.8.8.8.

params.name: host
params.description: The IP address or hostname to ping. Must be a bare host (e.g. 8.8.8.8, router.local, apple.com) — option-like or punctuated values are rejected.

params.name: count
params.description: How many echo requests to send (1–10). Defaults to 3.

name: dns_lookup
summary: Resolve a hostname to its IP addresses (A/AAAA records), or reverse-resolve an IP address to its hostname (PTR). Use to confirm DNS is working when names fail but IPs succeed.

params.name: host
params.description: The hostname to resolve (e.g. apple.com) or an IP address to reverse-resolve (e.g. 17.253.144.10). Must be a bare host — option-like or punctuated values are rejected.

name: listening_ports
summary: List the ports this Mac is listening on and which process (name + PID) owns each one. Answers 'what's using port N' and 'what's accepting connections on this machine'.

params.name: protocol
params.description: Which transport to report: tcp (listening TCP sockets, the default), udp (bound UDP sockets), or both.

name: lan_devices
summary: List other devices on the local network (IP + MAC address) from this Mac's ARP cache. Note: this only shows hosts this Mac has recently communicated with, not every device on the network — use scan_lan for a fuller sweep.

name: scan_lan
summary: Actively discover devices on the local network by pinging every address in this Mac's IPv4 subnet, then reporting the IP + MAC of every host that answered. More complete than lan_devices but slower and it generates network traffic, so choose it deliberately. Limited to /24-or-smaller subnets and bounded by the request timeout.
